title: Built Without an LLM: Pre-Reader Curriculum for Two Kids | vitalii.no
description:
The task engine behind Boytasks was built for kids who can already read instructions. A first-grader and his three-year-old brother can't, so dropping them into the same AI-generated routine either produced nothing usable or skipped straight to practice with no teaching step first. Worse, letters spoken by the text-to-speech voice came out as glyph names like 'ess' instead of the actual sound a child needs to hear to sound out a word.

For grade 2 and under, the generation step now writes a compact spec instead of calling an AI model, and the app builds every lesson on-device from local content banks: a letter progression modeled on a first-grade reading curriculum, first-sound and rhyme games, counting up to 20, and listen-and-tap English. Every subject opens with a scripted teach-first micro-lesson — hook, model, three examples, one guided try — that advances itself as the narration finishes rather than waiting for a tap. A phoneme map forces every letter to be spoken as its sound rather than its name, and a mastery loop tracks consecutive correct answers per skill, retiring items once they're mastered.

The older brother got a brand-new bonus round that didn't exist before, built locally so it costs no AI call, and the younger brother's session grew from a handful of toddler games to a full eight-item curriculum matched to his age.
